CREATION_RULE_CONTEXT.NETWORK_ENVIRONMENT_CONSTRAINTS: Deterministic self-contained grading runtime; authoring may reference official docs.ansible.com, grading must not require mutable internet access.

APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Recover a production-style Ansible fleet automation estate that provisions and reconciles application, proxy, observability, certificate, policy and secret-dependent configuration across heterogeneous node groups, using execution evidence to diagnose a chain of toolchain, project-discovery, variable, Vault, role-ordering, syntax and template failures until repeated runs converge safely.

APPROVED_OPERATIONAL_REQUIREMENTS: The supplied controller starts in an inherited legacy state and operational commands must expose enough evidence to diagnose compatibility before successful project bootstrap.
The project must use a project-local configuration and role layout, but starter discovery behavior must fail realistically until repaired.
Production roles must be materially differentiated across preflight, common baseline, identity, certificates, application, proxy, observability, policy and validation responsibilities.
Inventory/group/host variables must model multiple sites and environments with meaningful precedence and scoped overrides.
Sensitive application/proxy credentials must be represented through Ansible Vault-compatible encrypted content and must not appear in normal task output.
Role dependencies and ordering must encode prerequisites; starter defects may cause wrong order or wrong role execution, while the repaired run must converge deterministically.

Templates must perform non-trivial Jinja transformations including backend aggregation, endpoint normalization, site policy projection, secret references, monitoring targets and trust-bundle composition.
Malformed YAML/task syntax and template expressions must be realistic and diagnosable from Ansible parser/runtime logs rather than direct repair hints.
A failed preflight or render must preserve last-known-good rendered configuration; successful repeated execution must be idempotent.
Solver-visible incident artifacts must identify commands and log/evidence locations, not hidden root causes.
Official Ansible documentation references must come from docs.ansible.com and cover configuration generation, configuration settings, roles, variables, Vault and templating.
The grader must validate both fail-to-pass repairs and pass-to-pass preservation across independent behavior families.

STATE_MODEL.safety: Render to staged paths, validate, then atomically promote; failed validation preserves prior materialized state.

SOLVER_VISIBLE_DOC_PLAN: docs/operations.md with canonical commands and evidence paths
docs/official-ansible-references.md containing only official docs.ansible.com links/titles and provenance notes
runtime/logs/incident-bootstrap.log and incident-playbook.log captured from starter behavior
outputs.SCALE_FIT: large_system_strict: target 3,500-4,500 substantive solver-visible lines across differentiated Ansible, Jinja, inventory, Python validation helpers and operational fixtures; 24 defects from six coupled root-cause clusters; 27 F2P plus at least 8 P2P behaviors.
outputs.DATA_VOLUME_PLAN: Twelve deterministic localhost-backed fleet identities across three sites with differentiated host/group inputs; generated rootfs and evidence remain compact while exercising cross-host and rolling semantics.
